title: Notion system requirements mac: how to check your Mac, macOS version and chip
metaTitle: Notion System Requirements Mac: How to Check It
description: Notion system requirements mac, explained: the desktop app needs macOS 13 or later. Here is how to check your Mac, chip, and app version.
secondaryKeywords: Notion not supported on this Mac
intro: The Notion desktop app on Mac needs macOS 13 or above. To check your Mac, open Apple menu > About This Mac, confirm the macOS version and processor, then compare them with Notion's official requirements.
tldr: Notion's desktop app for Mac requires macOS 13 or above, according to Notion's help center.
Open Apple menu > About This Mac to read your macOS version and your processor.
Notion's official requirements list no chip, RAM, or disk minimum for the Mac app.
If Notion says it is not supported on your Mac, install the build that matches your processor.
Keep the app current with Notion > Check for Updates, and reload with ⌘ R if features are missing.

blocks.text: What Notion requires on a Mac

Notion publishes its system requirements in its help center, and the Mac part is short. The desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. That is the one hard number on the page for Mac users. If your Mac runs macOS 13 or newer, it meets the desktop requirement.
The same page does not list a required chip. It does not list RAM or disk space either. So you cannot check those three things against a published figure, because Notion does not publish one.
You will find older numbers online. Some third-party guides still say macOS 12 or an older 10.x release is the minimum. Those figures look outdated next to Notion's own page, so do not rely on them.

rows: The last eight major Extended stable releases
Web app in Firefox, Safari, or Edge
blocks.caption: Notion's official requirements, as listed on its help center. Read the Mac row first.

blocks.text: Read the Mac row first. The other rows matter only if you also use Notion on Windows, on a phone, or in a browser. Each platform has its own floor, and none of them replaces the macOS number.

Notion's help page also gives general advice. For the best experience, use the latest version of your operating system or browser. That is advice, not a hard limit. Updating now is cheaper than debugging a problem later.
Step by step: check your macOS version first

Start with your macOS version. Click the Apple logo at the top left of your screen, then choose About This Mac. The window shows your macOS version and your processor. Write both down before you go further.

Compare the version with 13. A Mac on macOS 13 or above meets Notion's desktop requirement. A Mac on macOS 12 or older does not, so the desktop app is not a supported option there. Use the web app in a supported browser instead.

Upgrade before you give up. Notion's page tells you to use the latest operating system. Open System Settings > General > Software Update and install any update that Apple offers. If the update brings you to macOS 13 or above, the desktop app becomes an option again.
Check your processor and the not supported error

The official help page covers one chip-related problem. You may see this message: "You can't open the application Notion because this application is not supported on this Mac." Notion says this happens when the downloaded build does not match your processor.

The fix is to uninstall the app, then install the version that matches your processor. Check the processor first in Apple menu > About This Mac, so you download the right build the first time. Reinstalling the same build will not help.

Notion's requirements page does not say which chips it supports. So the error message is your signal, not a published chip list. Do not guess from the year your Mac came out. Read the processor, then match the download to it.
Confirm Notion is up to date on your Mac
Notion updates the desktop app on its own. You can still check by hand. Click Notion in the menu bar, then click Check for Updates. Run this check when something looks wrong, not as a daily habit.
To see when the app last updated, click ? in the left sidebar, then click More. Use that date to judge whether your copy is recent. An old copy is the first suspect when a feature is missing.

If new features do not appear, reload the app with ⌘ R. Notion says this can usually force an update when none has arrived for a few days. Reloading takes seconds, so try it before you reinstall anything.

blocks.title: Updates are automatic
blocks.text: Notion says desktop updates happen on their own. Use Check for Updates when a feature is missing or the app acts oddly, not on a schedule.
Why the app version number is harder to find

Many guides promise a version number in one specific menu. Notion's help pages do not say where the version number appears. This guide does not give a path for it, because none was confirmed. Use the two checks that Notion documents instead.

The Homebrew cask listing for Notion shows version 7.42.3, which requires macOS 13 or above, as of 7 November 2026. Treat that as a reference point. The cask can lag behind the build Notion publishes on its own site.
RAM and disk space: what the requirements page leaves out
People often ask how much memory or storage Notion needs on a Mac. Notion's requirements page gives no figure for either. This guide will not invent one, and you should be wary of any site that does.

If Notion feels slow, the cause is usually something other than compatibility. A heavy workspace, a busy Mac, or a weak network can each slow a page. Those are performance questions, and their fixes differ from a requirements fix.

blocks.title: No published RAM or disk minimum
blocks.text: Notion's requirements page does not publish RAM or disk minimums for the Mac app. A number you find elsewhere is not an official Notion requirement.
When to use the web app instead

If your Mac cannot run the macOS 13 desktop app, Notion still works in a browser. The web app has its own support rules, and they depend on the browser. Chrome supports the last eight major Extended stable releases. Firefox, Safari, and Edge support the last two major releases.

Worked example: say About This Mac shows macOS 12. The desktop app is out. If you use Chrome, check that your version sits in its last eight major Extended stable releases. If you use Safari, check that it sits in the last two major releases.
Update the browser first, then retest the page you need. A browser older than those windows falls outside Notion's stated support, even if a page still loads. Loading is not the same as supported.
Windows, iPhone, and Android requirements in brief

This guide covers the Mac, but the same help page lists other platforms. The Windows desktop app needs Windows 10 version 21H2 or above. The mobile apps need iOS 17.0 or above on iPhone and Android 8 or above on Android.

The page also lists iPhone and iPad models that are not supported, and names iPhone 7, iPhone 6, and iPhone 6s. Check that list before you install on an older phone. Notion has no Linux app at the moment, so Linux users need the web app.
Mistakes people make when checking requirements

items: Trusting an old guide that says macOS 12 or 10.x is enough.
Reading the Homebrew version as the newest build of the app.
Reinstalling the same build when the processor does not match.
Looking for a RAM or disk minimum that Notion does not publish.
Giving up on Notion on an older Mac without trying the browser.

blocks.text: Each mistake wastes time. Check macOS 13 first, then the processor match, then the update status. That order rules out the common causes quickly, and it takes only a few minutes.
Keep Notion supported after a macOS upgrade
Apple and Notion release updates on their own schedules. A macOS upgrade can change what works. Check again after a major upgrade instead of trusting an old check.

Before you upgrade macOS, read Notion's requirements page again. The floor is a published number, and it can change. After the upgrade, open Notion, run Notion > Check for Updates, and open a page you use every day.

If the page loads and your blocks, databases, and comments behave as expected, your setup works. If something fails, reload with ⌘ R first, then check the processor match. Those two steps cover most problems in this area.
Mac details worth knowing once you are set up

The desktop help page mentions two Mac features. Command Search opens from the menu bar, so you can search your workspace without switching windows. You can also set Notion to launch at login from the Dock's Options menu.
Launch at login helps if you open Notion first thing each day. It has no effect on system requirements. Keep the two questions separate when you troubleshoot, so you do not chase the wrong fix.
Quick checklist before you install or upgrade

items: macOS 13 or above, confirmed in Apple menu > About This Mac.
A Notion download that matches your processor, from the same About This Mac window.
Notion > Check for Updates run once, with the app current.
A supported browser release, if you use the web app instead of the desktop app.

faq.question: What macOS version does Notion need on a Mac?
faq.answer: The Notion desktop app for Mac needs macOS 13 or above, according to Notion's official help center. Older guides that list macOS 12 or 10.x look outdated, so use 13 as your floor.

faq.question: Does Notion list a required Mac chip, RAM, or disk space?
faq.answer: No. Notion's system requirements page does not state an Apple silicon or Intel requirement, a RAM figure, or a disk space figure. If the app says it is not supported on your Mac, the downloaded build probably does not match your processor.

faq.question: How do I check my Mac's processor?
faq.answer: Click the Apple logo at the top left of the screen, then choose About This Mac. The window shows your processor. Use that to match the Notion download to your chip.

faq.question: How do I check for a Notion desktop update on Mac?
faq.answer: Click Notion in the menu bar, then click Check for Updates. To see when the app last updated, click ? in the left sidebar, then click More.

faq.question: Can I use Notion on a Mac that runs macOS 12?
faq.answer: Not with the desktop app, because the official requirement is macOS 13 or above. You can use Notion in a supported browser instead. Chrome must be among its last eight major Extended stable releases, and Firefox, Safari, or Edge must be among the last two major releases.

faq.question: Why is Notion slow on my Mac if my system meets the requirements?
faq.answer: The requirements page covers compatibility, not speed. Reload with ⌘ R, close heavy apps, and check your network. The official page gives no RAM or disk figure to compare your Mac against.

faq.question: Does Notion have a Linux app?
faq.answer: No. Notion's desktop help page says the company has no Linux app at the moment. Linux users need to use the web app in a supported browser.

faq.question: What does the Homebrew version number tell me?
faq.answer: Homebrew listed Notion version 7.42.3 with a macOS 13 requirement, as of 7 November 2026. The cask can lag the build on Notion's site, so treat the number as a reference point, not the newest release.

task: Check Notion system requirements on your Mac
appliesTo: Notion desktop app on a Mac running macOS 13 or later
requirements: A Mac running macOS 13 or above, or a supported browser for the web app
Access to the Apple menu and About This Mac
Notion desktop app installed, if you want to check for updates
An internet connection for Check for Updates and reloading

steps.name: Open the Apple menu
steps.text: Click the Apple logo at the top left of your screen. The Apple menu stays on the far left of the menu bar, even when Notion is in front.

steps.name: Open About This Mac
steps.text: Choose About This Mac. Read the macOS version and the processor, and write both down before you go further.
steps.tip: Notion's desktop floor is macOS 13 or above. Anything lower means the desktop app is not a supported option.

steps.name: Compare macOS with the requirement
steps.text: If your macOS version is 13 or above, your Mac meets Notion's desktop requirement. If it is 12 or lower, use Notion in a supported browser instead.

steps.name: Check the processor match
steps.text: If you saw the message that Notion is not supported on this Mac, uninstall the app. Then install the build that matches the processor you read in About This Mac.
steps.tip: Reinstalling the same build does not fix a processor mismatch. Check the processor before you download.

steps.name: Check for updates
steps.text: Click Notion in the menu bar, then click Check for Updates.

steps.name: See when the app last updated
steps.text: In the left sidebar, click ?, then click More. Read the date to judge whether your copy is recent.
steps.tip: Notion says desktop updates are automatic, so use this check when something looks wrong.

steps.name: Reload Notion
steps.text: Press ⌘ R to reload the app. Notion says this can usually force an update when none has arrived for a few days.

steps.name: Check your browser for the web app
steps.text: If you use the web app, check your browser version. Chrome must be among its last eight major Extended stable releases. Firefox, Safari, and Edge must be among their last two major releases.

troubleshooting.problem: Notion says it is not supported on this Mac
troubleshooting.fix: The downloaded build does not match your processor. Uninstall Notion, check the processor in Apple menu > About This Mac, then install the matching version.
Click Notion > Check for Updates, then reload with ⌘ R. Notion says a reload can usually force an update if none has arrived for a few days.

troubleshooting.problem: My Mac runs macOS 12 or older
troubleshooting.fix: The desktop app needs macOS 13 or above. Upgrade macOS if your Mac supports it. If not, use Notion in a supported browser release.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find the app version number
troubleshooting.fix: Notion's help pages do not say where the version number appears. Use the ? > More path in the left sidebar to see when the app last updated.

troubleshooting.problem: An old guide says macOS 12 is enough
troubleshooting.fix: Notion's official help page says macOS 13 or above. Use the official page, since older third-party numbers look outdated.
